Does Early Access to Social Media Harm Later Learning? New Evidence from Italy (by Marco Gui). Students who got social media accounts by age 12 progressed less than those who waited until age 14
Australia’s Social Media Policy Is Succeeding (by Ravi Iyer)
Why Did We Let Big Tech Take Over Education? (by Sophie Winkleman). Sophie Winkleman lays out the damage from the screen-based school day and shows how to roll it back.

What Does a 13-Year-Old See on Snapchat in a Normal Week? (by Brooke Istook). Two new studies show that kids and teens frequently encounter graphic violence, sexual content, and adult strangers on the app.
Teen Girls’ Suicide Rates Are Rising In Many Countries Around The World (by Jean M. Twenge). New analyses from Europe, Japan, and South Korea show increases that in many cases began before COVID.
Why You Should Be a Techno-Skeptic (by Jon Haidt). In his most urgent TED Talk yet, Jon Haidt reminds us that human connection is not optional.

The State of Childhood in the U.S. (by Lyman Stone). A new survey of U.S. parents by the Institute for Family Studies suggests that kids are still overprotected in the real world and underprotected online.
We Took Away the Phones — Now What?  (by Seth Kaplan). How rebuilding youth community groups can restore a play-based childhood.
Don’t Let Big Tech Hide Behind a Rainbow Flag (by Lennon Torres). Lennon Torres on why social media regulation is a prerequisite for LGBTQ safety.
The Case Against Social Media: Seven Lines of Evidence (by Jon Haidt). Your guide to the evidence that will help decide thousands of future court cases.
How Indonesia is Protecting 80 Million Children from Online Harm (by Anindito Aditomo). Their first-of-its-kind regulation cracks down on harmful design and incentivizes safer technology.

Phones at School: Less Learning, More Loneliness (by Jean M. Twenge). A new analysis shows the twin impacts of the leisure use of devices during the school day: declines in test scores and increases in feelings of loneliness at school.

This is another unexpected benefit of phone-free schools: big drops in # of fights and disciplinary referrals. I'm hearing this from so many schools. 
The constant drama and conflict on social media often leads to real-world fights. Shut it down for 7 hours a day.

Here's another example of overprotection in the real world: banning peanuts from schools caused kids antifragile immune systems to develop improperly, leading to peanut allergies, as @glukianoff and I wrote about. (Meanwhile no protections online)
One of the many delightful surprises coming in from newly phone-free schools:  Kids check out many more books from the library!

Many teachers say class is better when they get rid of the Chromebooks too. 

Multifunction devices guarantee distraction.  We need distraction-free schools. No phones, no Chromebooks.

Testimonials are coming in from teachers about their newly phone-free schools, and the amazing things that students are now doing. Like taking notes, completing their assignments, then talking to each other.

 "Was it this easy of a solution the whole time?"
